contents.support: Lee states that every Jacobi field is induced by a geodesic variation and leaves the proof as Exercise 10.1, with the exponential-map construction as a hint. The local proof supplies the initial-data calculation and common-domain argument.

contents.name: Proposition 10.4, Jacobi initial-value existence and uniqueness
contents.locator: Proposition 10.4 and proof, printed p.176 (PDF label P192)
contents.support: Lee constructs a parallel orthonormal frame, reduces the equation to a first-order linear system, and invokes Theorem 4.12 for solutions on all of I. Theorem 4.12's stated scope is any interval, but its proof is left as Exercise 4.11 at printed pp.60-61 / PDF P76-77; the local proof supplies the interval extension from the library's compact-interval matrix ODE theorem and unique gluing.

contents.name: Corollary 10.5, 2n-dimensional Jacobi space
contents.locator: Corollary 10.5 and proof following Proposition 10.4, printed p.176 / PDF label P192, lines 6905–6908; Proposition 10.4 proof at lines 6892–6904.
contents.support: Lee identifies the initial-data evaluation map as a bijection and concludes dimension 2n. The local proof additionally establishes the Jacobi-field vector-space structure, linearity of the map, and the product-basis dimension, and states the endpoint, zero-dimensional, and constant-geodesic scope.

contents.support: Lee verifies the velocity and parameter-multiple trivial Jacobi fields and proves the tangential/normal decomposition from the linearity of the velocity pairing. The item directly substitutes f times the velocity and proves both directions, including the constant-geodesic exception.

contents.name: Conjugate endpoints and order or multiplicity along a geodesic

contents.support: Lee defines conjugacy by a nonzero endpoint-vanishing Jacobi field and multiplicity as the dimension of that space. canonical.name: Sequential compactness of the unit sphere in a finite-dimensional normed space, and of the Riemannian unit tangent sphere
canonical.locator: Local synthesis of thm-closed-unit-ball-compact-iff-finite-dimensional and thm-compact-implies-the-other-compactness-forms; supplies the limiting-direction subsequence that Datar, Lemma 23.2.2 proof (printed pp.167-168), passes to without proof
canonical.support: The finite ordered basis of a finite-dimensional normed space makes the closed unit ball compact; compact metric spaces are countably compact and then sequentially compact, and the limit of a sequence of unit vectors has norm one by the reverse triangle inequality. This is the prerequisite used by thm-characterization-of-a-cut-point and by the later cut-locus closedness and cut-time continuity items.

canonical.name: Local length comparison for a conjugate-free geodesic (nearby-curve minimization with equality only up to monotone reparametrization)
canonical.locator: Zuoqin Wang, Riemannian Geometry (USTC, 2024 Spring), Lecture 20, Theorem 1.1(1) with its 'moreover' clause and Lemma 1.3 with proof (finite local inverse branches of exp_p, pull-back of a nearby curve, Gauss-lemma estimate, equality discussion); the smoothed-radius device and the full equality analysis are carried out locally
canonical.support: Covers the isolated length-minimizing property of a geodesic segment with no conjugate point to its initial point through the terminal time, including the equality case: equality of lengths forces the competitor to be the original geodesic composed with a continuous nondecreasing piecewise C^1 reparametrization. This is the prerequisite used by cor-a-geodesic-segment-before-its-first-conjugate-point-is-locally-energy-minimizing, which converts the length comparison into a strict local half-energy minimization.

canonical.name: Smoothness of the pointwise norm on a tangent space off zero
canonical.locator: Local synthesis: one ordered basis of T_pM turns the pointwise norm into the square root of the positive definite quadratic form q with constant coefficients g_p(e_i,e_j); polynomials are smooth by thm-ck-euclidean-maps-closed-under-algebra-and-composition, and the square root is smooth on (0,infinity) by thm-euclidean-inverse-function-theorem with thm-higher-regularity-of-local-inverses and thm-of-square-roots. The step is left implicit in Lee, Chapter 10, printed pp.173-190, and in Datar, section 23.3, printed pp.170-172
canonical.support: The norm |w|_g = sqrt(g_p(w,w)) equals sqrt(q(v(w))) in the coordinates of one fixed ordered basis; q is a positive definite quadratic polynomial, hence smooth with strictly positive values off zero, and the square root is smooth on (0,infinity) because it is the local inverse of t mapsto t^2 at every positive point. This is the prerequisite that makes r_p = N_p composed with the inverse of exp_p a smooth function on M minus ({p} union Cut(p)) in thm-distance-from-p-is-smooth-off-p-and-the-cut-locus.
